Client briefing · committed records as of 30 Sep 2026, 00:16 UTC

Daliesk

A pilot of an organisation of AI agents that changes a codebase through a ticket queue. Each change is made in its own working copy, must pass the ticket’s own acceptance checks, is approved by a separate reviewer that reads the change but not the session that made it, and is pushed to the development branch as one attributable commit; continuous integration then runs on the branch. Every step is recorded in the repositoryC.1Source C.1The shift engine as its Agent Note and the enterprise README describe it: a worktree per ticket, the ticket’s acceptance checks, a separate reviewer given the diff, the commit messages and the check output, one commit per ticket pushed to the development branch, Branch CI on the pushed tip, and the record each step leaves. .agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-28-enterprise-shift-engine.md · data/enterprise/README.md.

What is running

A cycle script and a scheduler that starts it are in place1.10Source 1.10The cycle and the scheduler as their scripts document them: one cycle every 2 hours, at 13 minutes past every even UTC hour, or when the operator starts one; intake when fewer than 8 tickets are open; a shift over the next 2 open tickets. These are the scripts’ defaults. data/enterprise/README.md · scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh · scripts/enterprise-scheduler.sh. Every two hours, at 13 minutes past an even UTC hour, the scheduler starts one cycle: intake refills the queue when fewer than 8 tickets are open, a shift works the next 2 open tickets, the divisions that need no ticket run their functions on the new branch tip, and the roster, the deck and this briefing are regenerated. The operator can also start a shift or a cycle by hand.

This is a pilot. The 11 tickets shipped so far came from shift 182951-78a6, started by the operator; cycle-20260929T001517Z, whose starter the records do not state; cycle-20260929T101300Z, started by the scheduler, whose push the supervisor completed (its ledger lines are recorded by the supervisor); cycle-20260929T121300Z, started by the scheduler; cycle-20260929T161300Z, started by the scheduler; and cycle-20260929T221300Z, started by the scheduler1.11Source 1.11Every cycle the branch names and every shift record outside all of them; a cycle's shifts are those its record lists, or the shift records that start between its start and the next cycle's (and before its shift step ended, when its captured log states that step); per unit, the tickets its shift records name, the ledger lines of those shifts by status, the named tickets no line records, and the lines' tokens. data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl · data/enterprise/shifts · data/enterprise/shift-starts.jsonl · data/enterprise/cycles · data/transcripts/live/enterprise-cycles · scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh · scripts/enterprise-scheduler.sh. 02

The operating model

Every seat is a role grounded in a real part of this repository2.1Source 2.1Per division: seats defined; seats with an attributed session or a ledger line; seats whose status is active. data/enterprise/roster.json. A person owns the queue policy, the schedule and the branch; the agents work inside those limits2.2Source 2.2How each division is engaged: the functions table and the cycle in the enterprise README, and the divisions that hold tickets in the queue README. data/enterprise/README.md · data/enterprise/tickets/README.md.

The organisation2.1Source 2.1Per division: seats defined; seats with an attributed session or a ledger line; seats whose status is active. data/enterprise/roster.json

A seat is a defined role: a package steward, a verification gate, a CI judge, a review department. It counts as occupied only when a recorded deliverable names it — a session, a ledger line, a CI verdict — and never by its definition alone. The tags show how each division receives work2.2Source 2.2How each division is engaged: the functions table and the cycle in the enterprise README, and the divisions that hold tickets in the queue README. data/enterprise/README.md · data/enterprise/tickets/README.md.

One ticket, from intake to the branch2.3Source 2.3The shift engine as its Agent Note and the enterprise README describe it, step by step, with the record each step leaves. .agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-28-enterprise-shift-engine.md · data/enterprise/README.md · data/enterprise/tickets/README.md

Each step is performed by a different actor and leaves its own record, so the path of any change can be read back from the repository. Continuous integration runs after the push; it reports on the branch and does not gate the change.

        04

        Measured quality

        How well the harness and the code-safety program perform, measured against tasks and targets whose answers are known.

        The Proving Ground benchmark

        The harness is measured on 444.1Source 4.1Environment directories carrying a task.json. examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/environments task environments across 64.2Source 4.2Distinct domain fields of those task.json files. examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/environments domains; the two hardest tiers are judged on hidden cases the implementer never sees. A frozen paired experiment runs the same cells under two arms that differ in one field and reads the difference with a bootstrap interval; its verdict is promote or reject only when the interval clears the plan’s thresholds. 224.3Source 4.3Records whose result.json carries a verdict, an interval and at least one paired cell. data/proving-ground frozen pairs are on record, and 34.4Source 4.4Frozen pairs whose current verdict (a re-read fold's when one exists) is promote or reject. data/proving-ground reached a decisive verdict.

        What the pairs show4.5Source 4.5Each frozen pair's result.json: delta, interval and verdict as recorded, certificates per arm as the sum of each cell's rate times its pairs, and a re-read fold's reading when one exists. data/proving-ground · data/proving-ground/folds

        • The model matters most. On tier 5 a larger model certified 16 of 16 cells against 13 for the middle model (+0.19, interval [0.13, 0.25], promote); a smaller one certified 1 against 14 (−0.81, interval [−0.88, −0.75], reject).
        • The harness loop and the product’s own loop are level on results. 15 against 14 of 16 sealed tier-5 cells (−0.06, interval [−0.13, 0.00], inconclusive); 40 against 40 of 40 on the public polyglot suite.
        • Retrying helps, by less than the first reading. Three attempts against one read −0.38, interval [−0.56, −0.19], reject in the first pair; the 2 replications read −0.06, interval [−0.13, 0.00], inconclusive and −0.06, interval [−0.19, 0.06], inconclusive.
        • No harness mechanism has been promoted. The largest mechanism reading, a self-review turn before validation, is +0.17, interval [−0.04, 0.38], inconclusive.
        • The instrument’s resolution. A repeat of the same 16 cells differs by about one cell, so one pair of 16 cannot resolve an effect smaller than about 0.194.6Source 4.6The results note: two sealed runs of the same arm agree on 15 of 16 cells, so a paired delta of one cell in sixteen is inside one arm’s own variation, and sixteen cells give an interval no narrower than about ±0.19. .agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-08-hypothesis-program-results.md.

        Security-review recall against documented defects

        The code-safety program reviews a codebase in six departments — secrets, injection, access, data, dependencies and platform — and a committed examiner rejects any finding whose cited line does not hold; a finding it passes is line-verified: the quoted text is at the cited line of the cited file, which does not show that the finding is a real defect. Every review sends the code it reads to the model API and commits records that quote it4.13Source 4.13Where a reviewed codebase and its records go: each movement of the data with the file that shows it, the terms of each destination, and what a client engagement needs first. docs/client/data-handling.md. Recall is read against targets whose defects are documented: OWASP NodeGoat, with 18 issues, and Damn Vulnerable Java Application (dvja), with 14. A documented issue counts as found when a finding cites its file within three lines of the issue’s lines4.7Source 4.7Each record's findings.json read against its target's ground truth: an issue is found when a finding cites its file within three lines of its range or of an alsoAt location. data/code-safety · data/code-safety/targets.

        Three ways to review the same application4.8Source 4.8Each tier's findings read against the ground truth by the same three-line rule; the single model's cost and time from its own metadata; the enterprise tier's from its record's manifest. data/code-safety/comparisons/2026-09-22-nodegoat · data/code-safety/targets/nodegoat.ground-truth.json

        Each tier ran once. On this small application one model in one pass found 15 of 18 documented issues, more than the enterprise’s 13; the scanner found 4. The single pass released 23 findings, unverified: nothing checked them against the code. The enterprise released 47, each line-verified, with a record of how every finding was reached; 15 of them land on no documented issue and are untriaged candidates, not established defects4.9Source 4.9The comparison’s authored reading: the tiers, the gap list and the three improvement iterations with their decisions. data/code-safety/comparisons/2026-09-22-nodegoat/README.md.

        Every review of OWASP NodeGoat, in order4.10Source 4.10NodeGoat records read against the 18-issue ground truth. data/code-safety · data/code-safety/targets/nodegoat.ground-truth.json

        The 10 reviews of the same revision without the diagnosed checklists found between 13 and 15 of 18 documented issues, each within three lines. A generalist department added nothing. Checklists written from a diagnosis of the enterprise’s misses on this application found 18 and 18 in their two runs against 14 and 15 without them, an in-sample reading, because the checklists were written from the application they were scored on; whether they transfer to another codebase is untested. On Damn Vulnerable Java Application (dvja) the review found 13 of 14.

        Planted defects in this repository’s own code4.11Source 4.11The record's seeded-recall reading as seeded-recall.mjs wrote it: planted canaries caught by the three-line rule, with a Wilson 95% interval. data/code-safety/2026-09-28-dsh-self-review/seeded-recall.json

        With no ground truth for a client’s code, recall is read by planting defects in a copy without telling the review. On this repository’s own packages the review caught 6 of 8 planted defects within three lines, 95% interval 0.41 to 0.93. Three of the planted sites carried no reachable defect; on the five that did, it caught five4.12Source 4.12The code-safety README: three of the eight planted sites wrap an already narrowed value and carry no reachable defect; on the five that do, the review caught five. data/code-safety/README.md.

        05

        Data handling, governance and audit

        Where a client’s code and the records of the work go, the controls on what an agent can read, run and ship, and the record that makes each action attributable.

        Where the data goes

        A shift runs on one review machine5.1Source 5.1A shift clones the development branch into a scratch directory, gives each department its own worktree of that clone, points the clone’s push address at an unreachable URL, and pushes once from it at the end. .agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-28-enterprise-shift-engine.md · data/enterprise/README.md. Four movements of data cross its edge; the arrows point the way the data moves.

        The repository’s visibility on GitHub is public5.5Source 5.5The visibility field of GitHub's answer to GET /repos/LBJLincoln/deepseek-harness. · github.com/LBJLincoln/deepseek-harness. A client’s code read by a department therefore reaches Anthropic’s model API under the operator’s Claude Code login, and the session logs and transcripts that hold it are published with the repository. Every movement of the data, the terms of each destination and what the repository does not record about them are on the data-handling page5.31Source 5.31The full data flow of a review: each movement of the data with the file that shows it, the terms of each destination, what the repository does not record about them, and what a client engagement needs first. docs/client/data-handling.md.

        Required before a client’s code is read

        • An Anthropic API organisation for the engagement, under a data processing agreement with zero data retention, in place of the operator’s login.
        • The records, session logs and transcripts of the engagement kept in a private repository, and the live capture pointed at it.
        • Data-use terms naming the client, the agreement, the purposes, the residency and the retention pinned on every session5.6Source 5.6Data-use terms pinned to a session at creation (client, agreement, purposes, residency, retention, redaction profile); the curator refuses to export without a redaction profile and withholds sessions whose terms do not admit the purpose. packages/governance/data-use/README.md · packages/governance/curator/README.md.

        Controls

        ControlMechanismEvidence on record
        Execution isolationShift departments, reviewers, intake and code-safety reviews run unconfined, as the host user: each department works in its own worktree of a scratch clone whose push address is unreachable, which contains a mistaken push but is not a sandbox, and nothing yet limits their network or the host files and credentials they can read5.9Source 5.9The shift README’s section on what is confined states that the unreachable push URL contains a mistaken push and is not a sandbox, that nothing controls network egress, and that a department’s shell reads whatever the host user can. The shift composition runs shell commands through the local bash provider, not the sandbox; each department works in its own worktree of a scratch clone and pushes through an origin whose push URL is unreachable; the Claude Code overlay states the edits and version-control commands a department may run without a prompt. examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-shift/cordis.yml · examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-shift/overlays/claude-code.cordis.yml · .agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-28-enterprise-shift-engine.md · examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-shift/README.md.         What the records support, and what they do not

        • Price per change is not recorded. Unknown6.1Source 6.1Unknown: the ledger records tokens and seconds; the route is a flat-rate subscription and no record carries a price per ticket. Currency per shipped ticket. data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl: every shift ran on a flat-rate subscription route, so a per-ticket price would be an estimate, and this briefing states none.
        • A single model pass is cheaper and faster, and unchecked. On the same application one pass took 113 s and cost $0.36 by its own accounting; the enterprise took 22 min 36 s on the subscription and had every finding checked at its cited line6.7Source 6.7Each tier's findings read against the ground truth by the same three-line rule; the single model's cost and time from its own metadata; the enterprise tier's from its record's manifest. data/code-safety/comparisons/2026-09-22-nodegoat · data/code-safety/targets/nodegoat.ground-truth.json.
        • Scale is not yet established. These means rest on 11 shipped tickets6.6Source 6.6The tokens and seconds fields of each shipped ticket's line: the department's and the review's model tokens and time. data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl; a cost model for a client queue needs a pilot measured the same way.

        07

        Limits and risks

        What the evidence does not show, and the risks a client should weigh.

        1. A pilot. 117.1Source 7.1Tickets shipped by the ledger lines of the shifts the operator started, directly or through a cycle. data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl · data/enterprise/shifts · data/enterprise/shift-starts.jsonl · data/enterprise/cycles · data/transcripts/live/enterprise-cycles · scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh · scripts/enterprise-scheduler.sh tickets have shipped, 2 of them from work the operator started. The cycles the scheduler started have shipped 87.2Source 7.2Tickets shipped by the ledger lines of the shifts of the cycles the scheduler started. data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl · data/enterprise/shifts · data/enterprise/shift-starts.jsonl · data/enterprise/cycles · data/transcripts/live/enterprise-cycles · scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh · scripts/enterprise-scheduler.sh, and a container reset erased the session logs of the shift of cycle-20260928T201148Z before it recorded its tickets, which the supervisor wrote to the ledger as abandoned afterwards7.3Source 7.3What the container resets of 2026-09-28 erased, stated from commits and files on the branch. data/transcripts/LOSSES.md.
        2. Shift work is not yet sandboxed. A department runs its commands unconfined in a worktree of a scratch clone that cannot push; the sandbox and the sealed workspace are in use on the bench only7.5Source 7.5The shift composition names the local bash and subprocess providers and no sandbox provider. examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-shift/cordis.yml · examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-shift/overlays/claude-code.cordis.yml.
        3. Continuous integration is not green. 297.6Source 7.6Completed runs whose conclusion is success. data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl · data/enterprise/shifts · github.com/LBJLincoln/deepseek-harness/actions/workflows/branch-ci.yml of 154 completed Branch CI runs passed. No run tested a shipped commit on its own (07.7Source 7.7Shipped commits with a Branch CI run on exactly that commit, rather than on a later commit that contains it. data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl · data/enterprise/shifts · github.com/LBJLincoln/deepseek-harness/actions/workflows/branch-ci.yml of 11). Of the 6 pushes that carried them, the containing run of 3 failed and of 3 was cancelled by a later push before a verdict.
        4. The name DeepSeek is provenance, not a supplier. This repository is a fork of an open-source agent harness that DeepSeek AI publishes under the MIT licence, which is why its name and its package scope carry DeepSeek; DeepSeek AI has not built, reviewed or endorsed Daliesk. No shift, review or intake request goes to a DeepSeek endpoint: they go to Anthropic, as the next item states. Only the Proving Ground bench has run open-weight models, DeepSeek’s among them, through OpenRouter7.4Source 7.4The README's provenance paragraph and its account of which models ran: every enterprise ticket line records Claude Code or no model, every intake and code-safety review ran on Claude Code, and the bench's tier 2 ran free open-weight models through OpenRouter. README.md · LICENSE · data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl.
        5. A client’s code would leave the machine. Every model request, with the files a department reads, goes to Anthropic under the operator’s Claude Code login, and the session logs and transcripts are published with a public repository7.8Source 7.8The departments’ route is the operator’s Claude Code installation, and the live capture publishes the operator’s and the departments’ transcripts to the branch. examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/enterprise-shift/overlays/claude-code.cordis.yml · packages/llm/llm-claude-code/README.md · data/transcripts/README.md. The requirements in section 5 come first.
        6. No person signs. The engine decides each shift’s spec freeze and release itself, and no person approves a change before it is pushed; the 5 records that hold sign-off events label the engine’s decisions with a principal of the kind “human”7.9Source 7.9Every signoff/recorded event in the shift and intake records' session logs, with its transition, principal id, declared kind and time, and every entry of the decisions their result.json states, with its transition, principal id and kind. data/enterprise/shifts · data/enterprise/intake.
        7. Data-use terms are not yet pinned on delivery work. Sessions that pin terms: code-safety 0 of 114, shift 0 of 53, intake 0 of 47.10Source 7.10Session logs under each family's sessions/ directories, and those carrying a dataUse/terms event. data/proving-ground · data/code-safety · data/enterprise/shifts · data/enterprise/intake.
        8. One vendor. 98% of the recorded sessions that made a model request ran on one route, claude-code (1,299 of 1,328); a route’s usage limit halts a shift7.11Source 7.11evidence.routes: the recorded sessions of the committed records per provider route, attributed to a seat or not. data/enterprise/roster.json.
        9. The benchmark is narrow. The tasks are written in-house; the harness measured runs an eight-tool build rather than the full shipped composition7.12Source 7.12The four-goals note: every harness-loop cell on record ran an eight-tool build under a two-sentence persona, and the bench’s 44 tasks are hand-authored JavaScript programs, saturated below tier 5. .agents/notes/proposed/process/2026-09-22-four-goals-rethink.md; and no harness change has been promoted by a frozen pair7.13Source 7.13The results note: the tasks are authored in-house; sixteen cells per arm; no frozen pair has promoted a harness change. .agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-08-hypothesis-program-results.md.
        10. Security recall is read on training applications. The documented-defect targets are public, intentionally vulnerable applications; the checklist gain may not transfer; the review of this repository’s own code confirmed none of its findings and missed a defect its triage found7.14Source 7.14The comparison’s own caveat on the checklists, and the self-review’s triage: none of its findings confirmed, a Windows executable-search defect found by the triage and missed by the review. data/code-safety/comparisons/2026-09-22-nodegoat/README.md · data/code-safety/targets/README.md.
        11. A developer preview. The harness underneath is in developer preview and will change incompatibly7.15Source 7.15The repository README: DeepSeek Harness is in developer preview, with compatibility-breaking changes to come. README.md.

        08

        Roadmap and engagement

        The work that closes the limits above, and a proposed way to start with a client.

        Roadmap

        1. Data handling before any client work. Serve the departments from an Anthropic API organisation under a data processing agreement with zero data retention, keep the records in a private repository, and pin data-use terms on every session8.1Source 8.1The dataUse/terms fields a session pins at creation: client, agreement, purposes, residency, retention and redaction profile. packages/governance/data-use/README.md.
        2. Sign-off and isolation. Have a person sign each release after the certificate, under a principal the engine does not configure8.2Source 8.2The four-goals note’s proposal: task supply first (public suites, the completion family, a SWE-bench subset), more than one route, and a release signature recorded after the certificate by a principal the driver did not invent. .agents/notes/proposed/process/2026-09-22-four-goals-rethink.md; run shift departments under the sandbox the bench already uses.
        3. Unattended delivery, measured. Clear the doc-sync and coverage checks that halted the scheduled cycles’ tickets and make Branch CI green, then count what cycles ship without an operator, in the table of section 38.3Source 8.3Every cycle the branch names and every shift record outside all of them; a cycle's shifts are those its record lists, or the shift records that start between its start and the next cycle's (and before its shift step ended, when its captured log states that step); per unit, the tickets its shift records name, the ledger lines of those shifts by status, the named tickets no line records, and the lines' tokens. data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl · data/enterprise/shifts · data/enterprise/shift-starts.jsonl · data/enterprise/cycles · data/transcripts/live/enterprise-cycles · scripts/enterprise-cycle.sh · scripts/enterprise-scheduler.sh.
        4. Evidence that others can check. Measure on public suites and on private tasks no model has seen, with more cells per arm, before promoting any harness change8.2Source 8.2The four-goals note’s proposal: task supply first (public suites, the completion family, a SWE-bench subset), more than one route, and a release signature recorded after the certificate by a principal the driver did not invent. .agents/notes/proposed/process/2026-09-22-four-goals-rethink.md.
        5. More than one model vendor. Run the same cells on more routes, so a result is not one vendor’s8.2Source 8.2The four-goals note’s proposal: task supply first (public suites, the completion family, a SWE-bench subset), more than one route, and a release signature recorded after the certificate by a principal the driver did not invent. .agents/notes/proposed/process/2026-09-22-four-goals-rethink.md.
        6. Full CI coverage. Compose the Windows and primary lanes this fork lacks, so the vacant judge seats rule on real runs8.4Source 8.4The vacancy table names what changes when a Windows runner, a primary pool, an OTLP collector or a session store is composed. data/enterprise/README.md.

        Proposed engagement

        1. Step 1Data handling, terms and scope

          An Anthropic API organisation for the engagement under a data processing agreement with zero data retention; a private repository for the records; the data-use terms each session will pin; and the people who sign8.1Source 8.1The dataUse/terms fields a session pins at creation: client, agreement, purposes, residency, retention and redaction profile. packages/governance/data-use/README.md.

        2. Step 2A code-safety review of a codebase the client selects

          Six departments, each finding checked at the line it cites, the report with executive summaries in French and English; recall read by planting defects in a copy8.5Source 8.5Seeded-defect recall: plant known defects in a copy of a target without telling the review, and read the share it catches within three lines, with a Wilson interval. data/code-safety/README.md · data/code-safety/tools/seed-defects.mjs. On the reference application one review took up to 28.8 min8.6Source 8.6The largest elapsedSeconds over the manifest.json of every code-safety record. data/code-safety.

        3. Step 3Supervised shifts on an agreed queue

          Tickets under the client’s own acceptance commands, a person signing each release, measured as this briefing measures: checks, reviews, CI verdicts, tokens and time per ticket8.7Source 8.7The ticket validator takes its queue policy as a parameter: this repository’s policy mandates its typecheck and coverage runs; the open policy mandates nothing beyond the ticket’s own checks. scripts/enterprise-tickets.ts · .agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-28-enterprise-shift-engine.md.

        4. Step 4Decision

          Continue, widen or stop on the measured record, not on this document.
